nodes.title: Lock server + clients, mutual exclusion via a numeric token invariant over mailbox counts
Extend core with spawn/links first, then examples
Build Lean-to-Elixir emitter now
Do the lock example first: if cross-actor invariants are not tractable, more BEAM fidelity is pointless
Add Count.lean: mcount, deliver/set lemmas, Step.chars characterization, Reach.inv, Step.prefix
Count.lean proven: Step.chars gives states+counts per step, zero sorry
Write Examples/Lock.lean: lock server + clients, numeric token invariant, bounded model check before proof
Invariant holds on 64k configs (2 clients, depth 9) and 22k (3 clients, depth 7) incl. arbitrary env ticks; Inv.mutex proven
Invariant does not need FIFO: the non-FIFO case (acquire h while h still holder) is absorbed by a+qn=w. Suggests many BEAM protocols are FIFO-agnostic for safety
nodes.description: While designing the numeric token invariant I expected to need Step.prefix (FIFO). Instead the a+qn=w equation handles the out-of-order case. FIFO matters for liveness (the token is not lost), not for mutual exclusion.

nodes.title: Prove Inv preserved by every Step via Step.chars + omega case analysis
Inv.step proven: ~450 lines, zero sorry. Client half ~150 lines, server half ~250. Every case is Step.chars + simp on singleton counts + omega
Proof cost driver was not the protocol but Lean plumbing: if-then-else on pids, singleton List.count, and subst renaming. A tactic that normalises Step.chars output would cut the proof in half
nodes.description: Errors across iterations: by_contra missing (no Mathlib), cases pattern arity, subst replacing a def-valued pid, List.count on singletons not reduced by default simp, match on srv catch-all not reducing without cases on the Option. None were about the invariant, which the bounded model check had already validated.

nodes.title: Add EnvStep/ReachEnv (ticks at any time), Inv (initCfg n), end-to-end mutex_forever theorem
mutex_forever proven: from initCfg n under any interleaving of Steps and env ticks, two holding clients are the same pid. Zero sorry, zero warnings
Write elixir/lock.exs: same protocol on BEAM, random ticks, event-log overlap check
5 clients/2000 ticks and 20 clients/20000 ticks: max 1 holder, 0 violations
Mutation test: break the release-sender check in beh and confirm the bounded checker finds a violating trace
Grant-while-held caught at 279 configs, duplicate-acquire (token loss, mutex still holds) caught at 59 via Inv, no-sender-check unreachable: identical 64303-config state space

The invariant is stronger than the property: it catches the lost-token bug that mutual exclusion alone misses, and it identifies which defensive checks are load-bearing (none of the sender checks are, with honest clients)
nodes.description: First two mutants I wrote (no sender check on release; release on any message while holding) were both unreachable under honest clients and explored the same state space as the original. The invariant predicted this: r c p = 0 for non-holders, and no grant reaches a holding client. Replaced with grant-while-held (mutex violation) and duplicate-acquire (Inv violation only).

nodes.title: Elixir -> Lean translator driven by @type/@spec (Elixir is source of truth)
Lean -> Elixir emitter from a DSL (Lean is source of truth)
Liveness first: token never lost under fair scheduling, needs FIFO
Spawn/links/exits in the core
Elixir -> Lean translator using typespecs for the Lean inductives; first give Behavior access to self() so the translation is honest
Refactor core: Behavior σ μ := Pid → σ → μ → σ × sends (self pid); drop me from Lock client state; re-prove
Refactor done in one build: Behavior is Pid -> σ -> μ -> ...; Lock proof lost the cli field and ~20 lines; all examples and mutants unchanged in output
Write elixir/to_lean.exs: parse @type + handle_cast/handle_info clauses into Lean inductives and a Behavior
to_lean.exs (~330 lines) translates lock.ex and bank.ex; generated Lean compiles; drivers run the same sources on BEAM

The @type declarations were sufficient as the type oracle: Option wrapping, none/nil, list cons, enum atoms, and the non-linear pattern {p, [n|rest]} all resolved from types alone. No @spec needed beyond msg/state
nodes.description: Type-directed decisions in the translator: variable at Option position already bound at base type -> some x' with guard; nil at Option -> none; atom at enum type -> constructor; {:noreply, v} with v : Int at Option Int -> some v. Guards become if-then-else with fallthrough to the next subsuming clause; subsumed clauses are dropped since Lean rejects redundant alternatives.

nodes.title: Prove Gen.Lock.beh = Lock.beh and Gen.Bank.beh = Bank.beh; hand models adopt generated types
beh_eq_gen proven for Lock and Bank by funext+cases+rfl. Chain is now: lock.ex --to_lean--> Gen.Lock.beh = Lock.beh --Inv.step--> mutex_forever
The equivalence proof was one line per model. Guard orientation (p = p') and clause order were the only things that had to match; field names and redundant catch-alls did not matter
Progress: a waiting client is never stuck; either some actor can step or someone is in the critical section waiting on the environment
Full liveness under fair scheduling with a ranking function
Deadlock freedom as a safety property derived from Inv, strengthened with holder=none -> queue=[]
Deadlock freedom from Inv; full liveness deferred (needs fairness machinery, no Mathlib)
Add queue_empty field to Inv, prove Enabled-or-holding theorem and mcount_pos -> Step exists
progress + progress_forever proven in ~50 lines using only Inv (plus the new queue_empty field). No FIFO needed here either

For this protocol FIFO is not needed for safety or deadlock freedom. It would only matter for a fairness argument (bounded waiting), which needs a ranking function and a fair scheduler. Step.prefix exists but is unused by any example
nodes.description: Earlier I predicted FIFO would be needed for liveness. The deadlock-freedom proof went through with Inv alone. The invariant's a+qn=w equation absorbs message reordering. Bounded waiting (a queued client is granted within k releases) is where queue order and hence FIFO would enter.

nodes.title: handle_call support in the translator: server replies and client-side blocking calls
Server side only: handle_call/3 + {:reply,r,s} -> message with from pid + reply message; callers must be async
Also client side: split a clause at GenServer.call into an await state + resume-on-reply clause; defer other messages by re-enqueue to self
Add selective receive to the core Step relation
Both server and client side via CPS split with re-enqueue deferral; keep the core mailbox model unchanged
Extend to_lean.exs: @type call/reply, handle_call clauses, {:reply,..}, v = GenServer.call(...) CPS split, await constructors

handle_call works end to end: bank.ex uses handle_call/3 and a client blocking in GenServer.call; translated, beh_eq_gen holds, driver matches Lean trace (0, 9, 0); deferred-tick run ends at 15 on both bank and client

Await states are generated St constructors carrying the continuation's free variables; the reply type is a single shared Msg.reply. Limits: one @type reply per program, call must be an assignment statement, continuation cannot itself block (no nested awaits yet)
nodes.description: CPS split implemented in cps_split/6: captured = free vars of the rest that are bound in env. Nested/second blocking calls in the continuation would need recursion into plain_body with a fresh await index; not implemented. Also 'from' is a Lean keyword: added lean_ident sanitizer.

nodes.title: Re-enqueue deferral spins under an unfair scheduler (tick bounces until the reply lands). Harmless for safety proofs, blows up bounded exploration depth, and would need a fairness assumption for liveness
nodes.description: Alternative encodings: a per-actor deferred list in the Actor structure (closer to BEAM's save queue) would keep Step.queue but change Config; rejected for now to keep all existing proofs intact.

nodes.title: Follow-ups: nested awaits in the translator; lock clients acquire via blocking GenServer.call so the CPS split meets the mutex proof

nodes.title: Translator: recursive cps_split (nested awaits), pattern LHS for blocking call, GenServer.reply/2, GenServer.from() type, {pid,_} from-patterns at Pid positions, 3-arg call
Rewrite lock.ex: handle_call(:acquire) with deferred reply via GenServer.reply on release; clients block; regenerate; re-prove mutex + progress
Translator: nested awaits (client_await2 captures a), pattern LHS (:ok = call), GenServer.reply, GenServer.from, {pid,_} from-patterns, 3-arg call, single-atom types. Bank audit = 14 on Lean and BEAM

Lock with blocking acquire: Inv unchanged in shape (await state = waiting), model check 77925/23281 configs clean, Inv.step re-proven (685 lines, macros cut the client half in half), mutex_forever + progress_forever hold, mutants unchanged, BEAM run clean

The CPS split did not change the invariant at all: only the view (locOf) that maps the generated await constructor to 'waiting'. Blocking calls are a compilation detail of the client, not a protocol change
nodes.description: Predicted the mutex proof would need rework for the await state; in practice the six counters and two equations were untouched. The rework was mechanical: three client shapes instead of two phases, reply .ok instead of grant, and the deferral clause is a frame case (popped message re-sent to self does not touch any counted message).

nodes.title: Bounded waiting / FCFS: a client queued at rank k acquires the lock after exactly k handovers; FIFO becomes load-bearing
Full liveness with a fair scheduler and ranking function
FCFS as a trace-safety property: rank decreases by exactly one per handover while queued; needs 'holder never queued', which needs mailbox order (release h precedes acquire h)
FCFS via two new Inv fields: ordered (no acquire h before release h in server mailbox) and holder_not_queued; plus a Waiting trace relation counting transfers
Count.lean: exact mailbox equations (mboxOf_deliverAll_eq, sendsTo) and mailbox clause in Step.chars

Count.lean: sendsTo, mboxOf_deliverAll_eq, mcount_eq_of_mboxOf; Step.chars now also gives the exact mailbox equation. Lock.lean: relBeforeAcq with tail/head/append lemmas, two new Inv fields; model check clean on 77925/23281 configs
LockProof: preserve ordered and holder_not_queued in every case; the A2 case (acquire h while h holds) closes only via relBeforeAcq_head

LockProof preserves ordered and holder_not_queued in all cases; the A2 case closed via relBeforeAcq_head + token arithmetic. LockFcfs: Step.rank_step, Waiting relation (steps + env), bounded_waiting, fcfs. Zero sorry, zero warnings, chain passes

FIFO is finally load-bearing, and in exactly the place predicted three sessions ago: the reorder 'acquire h while h holds' is harmless for safety and deadlock freedom but breaks rank accounting. The proof that excludes it uses only the tail-append shape of Step.chars' mailbox clause
nodes.description: The ordered field is an invariant over the server's mailbox *list*, not counts. Preservation needed exact mailbox equations (mboxOf_deliverAll_eq) rather than mcount. The general append lemma relBeforeAcq_append handles every send with one side condition: appending release h requires no pending acquire h, which follows from hd=1 -> a=0 in the token invariant.

nodes.title: Spawn, links and exits in the core, with a supervisor example proven
Rewrite Config/Step in place with effects; re-prove Props/Count/all examples

New layer Sys over Config: next-pid counter, link list, pending exit signals; effects list per step; exit propagation as asynchronous signal steps (no recursion); conservativity theorem for message-only behaviours
Synchronous cascade on exit (recursive kill of linked non-trapping actors)
Sys layer with asynchronous exit signals; trapping is a predicate on state (Process.flag); EXIT delivered via a user codec exitMsg; lift theorem keeps every existing result valid
Write Leanactors/Sys.lean: Effect, EBehavior, Signals, Sys, runE/signalE, SysStep, lift + conservativity
Sys.lean built first try: Effect/EBehavior/Signals/Sys, runE/signalE, SysStep/SysReach, runSys_sound, lift + runE_lift conservativity
Supervisor example: one-for-one with trapping sup, worker exit error/normal, Inv = sup alive ∧ (child alive+linked ∨ signal pending ∨ EXIT in mailbox); bounded checker over runs, signals, env

Model check: 236220 configs clean at depth 9 / 4 env msgs. Mutant without trap_exit caught in 40 configs: sup dies on the child's crash signal. Trace: after crash+signal+restart, child=2, restarts=1, links=[(0,2)]
Prove Inv preserved by SysStep (run sup / run worker / run other / signal) and SysReach from init
Do both follow-ups, translator first so the lock rewrite can use nested awaits
Lock rewrite first, add nested awaits only if it needs them
Translator first, then lock; the lock is the integration test for the translator features
SupervisorProof done: Inv.frame (monotone) + Inv.terminate_ne cover every SysStep case; supervisor_alive and restart_in_flight from init. Zero sorry, zero warnings, chain passes

The proof cost of the new layer was in two reusable lemmas, not in the cases: 20 of 22 cases are 'apply frame' or 'apply terminate_ne' with trivial side goals. Asynchronous signals made the terminate lemma a plain record computation
nodes.description: Iterations were about Lean plumbing again: constructor field order in cases patterns, apply with rfl arguments unifying the wrong record, missing Nat. prefixes without Mathlib. None about the invariant, which the 236k-config check had validated.

nodes.title: Translator does not yet emit spawn_link/trap_exit/exit; the supervisor is hand-modelled. Next translator increment: Process.flag(:trap_exit) -> Signals.traps, spawn_link(Mod, f, args) -> spawnLink with the module's state constructor, exit(reason) -> exit
Translate the supervisor from Elixir: GenServer.start_link as spawnLink, Process.flag(:trap_exit) as Signals.traps, exit/{:stop,..} as exit effects
Effects mode in the translator, switched on per file when any handler spawns/exits/traps; message-only files keep emitting Behavior
Always emit EBehavior and use lift-free proofs everywhere
Per-file effects mode; Bank and Lock outputs stay byte-identical
Write elixir/src/supervisor.ex; extend to_lean.exs with effects mode, :EXIT typing, spawn aliases to fresh, exit reasons; generate Gen/Supervisor.lean

Effects mode in to_lean.exs: supervisor.ex translates to exactly the hand model; beh_eq_gen by cases+rfl; proof unchanged except EXIT rename; bank/lock outputs byte-identical; BEAM driver: crash -> restart, restarts=1

All three examples now come from Elixir source. Translator subset: casts, calls with blocking clients, replies, spawn_link, trap_exit, exit; ~600 lines, still unverified, always checked by an equivalence theorem against the hand model
nodes.description: The equivalence theorems are the trust boundary: beh_eq_gen for Bank, Lock, Supervisor. A translator bug shows up as a failed rfl, not as a false theorem.

nodes.title: Monitors: one-directional DOWN notifications, in Sys and the translator, with an async-task example proven
Monitors as a second list in Sys; terminate queues DOWN signals that are always delivered as messages via a downMsg codec; no cascade
Encode monitors as links plus trap_exit on the monitoring side
Separate monitor list and DOWN codec; the signal queue carries a kind tag (exit vs down)
Extend Sys.lean: Effect.monitor/spawnMonitor, Sys.monitors, SigKind, downMsg; keep runE_lift
Sys monitors done: watchers/unmonitor, terminate queues DOWN, downE delivers via optional codec; SysChoice; supervisor proof gained a 12-line down case; all green

Task example from Elixir: caller GenServer.start + Process.monitor a worker; worker replies then stops or crashes; translator: GenServer.start, Process.monitor, {:DOWN, ref, :process, pid, reason} typing, downMsg codec

Task translated exactly as designed (spawn + monitor as two effects, DOWN typed (Pid, Reason), downMsg codec generated). Model check 243526 configs clean; no-monitor mutant caught; BEAM driver: completed job counted, crashed job cleared, caller alive
TaskProof: Inv.frame + Inv.terminate_ne again, plus a none_case shape for the caller clearing its pending job; signal case closed by signals_nil

TaskProof done: frame/cleared/terminate_ne shapes; 22 cases; signal case closed by signals_nil; job_never_lost from init. Property-level mutant check: unmonitored crash loses the job at config 20. Chain passes with four drivers

Four examples now translate from Elixir and each has an invariant proof with the same recipe: bounded check, then frame lemma + termination lemma + one example-specific shape. Per-example proof cost is now ~300 lines and mostly cases that are one 'apply'
nodes.description: Bank (per-actor), Lock (cross-actor + FCFS), Supervisor (links/exits), Task (monitors). Recurring pitfalls: apply with hypotheses about the source forces the target to unify with it; use bullets.

nodes.title: Timers and remote exit signals: send_after / GenServer timeouts / Process.exit(pid, reason), with a watchdog example proven

Timers as a pending list; a timer step fires any pending timer (order nondeterministic, durations abstracted); GenServer {:noreply, s, t} as a self-timer that may fire even after a message arrived (sound over-approximation)
Model time explicitly with a clock and durations
Untimed timers: any pending timer may fire at any step; Process.exit(pid, r) queues an exit signal like a link would
Sys: timers list, Effect.sendAfter, Effect.signal, timerE step; extend supervisor/task proofs with the timer case
Timers and Effect.signal in Sys; SysStep.timer; both existing proofs extended with a 12-line frame case; all green first build

Watchdog example: pings a linked worker with a GenServer timeout, Process.exit(w, :kill) on timeout, restart on EXIT; translator: send to registered name, {:noreply, s, t}, Process.send_after, Process.exit, booleans

Watchdog translated (registered-name send, {:noreply,s,t}, Process.exit, booleans, named wildcards, pid-narrowed Option patterns, per-module catch-alls). Model check 10365 configs clean; no-trap mutant caught at 749; BEAM driver: hung worker killed by timeout, new worker running

BEAM subtlety the untimed model hides: any message resets a GenServer timeout, including :sys.get_state polls. The driver never saw the timeout until it stopped polling. In the model a timeout may fire regardless, which is the safe direction
nodes.description: Untimed timers over-approximate: the model admits a timeout firing after a pong. The real system under-fires when the mailbox is busy. Safety proofs hold in both; liveness of the watchdog (a hung worker is eventually replaced) would need the timer to actually fire, i.e. a fairness assumption on timers plus quiet mailboxes.

nodes.title: WatchdogProof: frame with child-preserving flag change, spawn shape with three effects, terminate_ne; signal/down/timer cases as before

WatchdogProof done: frame lets the flag change while the child is preserved; spawn shape with three effects; flag_case handles no-op and pong (deliver) and timeout (signal queued); all cases green on the 3rd build. watchdog_alive and restart_in_flight from init. Chain passes with five examples

Five translated examples cover the everyday BEAM toolbox: cast, call, reply, spawn/spawn_link, link, monitor, trap_exit, exit, Process.exit, send_after/timeouts. Each proof follows the frame+terminate recipe; the per-example novelty is one lemma
nodes.description: Remaining fidelity gaps are semantic, not syntactic: crash-on-unhandled-cast, real time, selective receive beyond call/reply, non-identity init, multi-node. All are recorded in the README.
